extracted.intended_audience: Early-career researchers (UCL) preparing applications for the Royal Society University Research Fellowship (URF)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting a Royal Society University Research Fellowship application, including eligibility, research remit, funding details, application process, and practical tips for using the flexi-grant system.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a PhD, applicants who have just submitted their PhD will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must already hold the PhD at time of application; 'just submitted' is not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-PhD research experience window
rubrics_metrics.description: Be at an early stage of their research career with between three to eight years of actual research experience since their PhD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count actual research experience since award of the PhD; the scheme targets researchers 3–8 years post-PhD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment status restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Not hold a permanent post in a university or not for profit research organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not already have permanent positions that imply stable independent employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous nationally competitive fellowship exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Not hold or previously have held a nationally competitive fellowship that provides an opportunity to establish an independent research group and therefore independent researcher status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have already held a fellowship that established you as an independent group leader you are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and visa responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All nationalities are welcome to apply - however you are responsible for any visa arrangements - Research and Innovation talent visa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International applicants may apply but must arrange any necessary visas themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research remit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research must be within the Royal Society Biological and Physical Sciences remit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The remit is divided into nine sectional committees; ensure your project maps to one of these areas (listed explicitly on the briefing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional committees (allowed research areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nine sectional committees: Pure and applied mathematics and computer science; Astronomy and physics, theoretical physics and applied physics; Chemistry, applied chemistry and theoretical chemistry; Engineering, technology, instrumentation, materials science and experimental fluid dynamics; Earth sciences and environmental physical sciences; Biochemistry, structural biology and molecular cell biology; Developmental biology, genetics, immunology, microbiology and experimental medical microbiology; Anatomy, physiology, neurosciences, health and human sciences; Organismal biology, evolutionary and ecological science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories when choosing keywords and indicating the appropriate selection committee for your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host location requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be held at a UK University or research institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship and host institution must be UK-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and start
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is initially provided for 5 years. Fellowships start from 1 October 2019 (scheme-specific start dates apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project timeline and recruitment/training around the fellowship duration and official start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and FEC coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: 80% of the research fellow’s salary costs (must not exceed £40,354.58), directly allocated costs (inc estate costs) and indirect costs under the FEC model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget accordingly; salary coverage is capped and follows Full Economic Costing (FEC) rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research assistance funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Research assistance 80% FEC of a PD/PDRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may request funding for a postdoc or PD at 80% FEC; include justification in the proposal and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research expenses coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: 100% research expenses including consumables and travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumables and travel can be requested at 100% of the cost; detail these in the expenses section.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD studentship contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: 4 year new PhD studentship (2 year contribution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship can include a new 4-year PhD studentship with the Royal Society contributing for 2 years; include supervisory and training plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment cost threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment - check the advice around the necessary contributions if this exceeds £10,000 (inc VAT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If equipment requested exceeds £10,000 (including VAT), follow specific advice about host contributions and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public engagement - something the Royal Society are really keen on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for public engagement and dissemination; this is viewed favorably by the funder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training support
rubrics_metrics.description: Training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe training for yourself and any staff/students supported by the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission route and system
rubrics_metrics.description: Round opens and applications are filled in via flexi-grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applications must be submitted through the flexi-grant portal; select the correct scheme and follow online instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional approver and referee submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: HoD and nominated referees submit their support via flexi-grant. Host Organisation’s approver submits their approval via flexi-grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure HoD, referees and the host organisation approver are registered on flexi-grant and submit required statements before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard deadline and non-submission consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline 5 September 3pm. Non submissions are rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deadline is strict; incomplete or late submissions will be rejected. Plan internal approvals accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and review stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility checks. Initial office based rejections. Shortlisted by URF selection panel. Independent referees score and comment on the proposals. Interviews held around April. Final decision at Selection Panel Meeting in May.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of multiple review stages (administrative checks, panel shortlisting, external referees, interviews) and prepare materials suited to each stage (e.g., concise lay summary for panel, detailed responses for referees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft to remit and avoid reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Individually craft the proposal to reflect its suitability against the Royal Society scientific remit. Don’t just copy and paste chunks of other fellowship applications, ensure the questions are answered appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor wording and emphasis to the URF remit and the specific sectional committee; answer each question directly rather than reusing text from other applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a strong justification for independence and give evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show evidence you are establishing an independent research programme (distinct from former supervisors, leadership potential, independent outputs, grant-getting capability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address public engagement clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider public engagement and how you will get your research out there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete engagement activities and plans for dissemination as part of the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords and committee fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords - use relevant overarching fields and more specific words - also use the area of the selection committee your research fits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose keywords to clearly indicate subject area and the appropriate sectional committee; use both broad and specific terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and lay explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: No jargon! The selection committee is made up of a wide range of fellows and relevant researchers/ RS Staff. It is likely this will not include experts in your field. Make the application easy to read, explain acronyms etc. Pay careful attention to the lay terms explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible summaries and avoid technical jargon; define acronyms and include a clear lay summary for non-specialists on the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: References currency and selectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: If including references use key ones and include up to date references to reflect the timeliness of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite essential, recent literature rather than exhaustive bibliographies; demonstrate awareness of current state-of-the-art.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you have an ORCID identifier and that your profile is up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register and maintain an up-to-date ORCID record before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications entry guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it says up to 3 publications always give 3 if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use all available publication slots to showcase your best and most relevant outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional committee spread consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society looks to spread URFs across the Sectional Committees - some areas are more under subscribed eg astronomy, engineering, mathematics and computing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awareness of committee-level supply/demand may inform timing or emphasis, but do not misrepresent your work's fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to under-represented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Under-represented groups are particularly encouraged to apply'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusivity statement; eligible applicants from under-represented backgrounds are welcomed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal research compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If using animals make sure you read the Royal Society statement on this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow funder policy and provide appropriate ethical approvals and justifications if animal work is proposed (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check referees and departmental approver early
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you check up on your referees and HoD. Provide advanced warning to your participants, warn them in advance that they will receive correspondence from the Royal Society - periodically check the spam filter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact referees and approvers well before the deadline; ensure they register on flexi-grant and submit letters promptly; remind them to mark and submit their parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexi-grant registration and data correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: You must register and ensure you fill in all the contact information correctly. Give a most up to date email and periodically check your spam folder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect contact details can block communications; use an email you check regularly and monitor spam/junk folders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select correct scheme and answer compulsory questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once logged in ensure you select the correct scheme to apply for. Provide answers to all the questions where applicable and particularly where marked with an * as these are compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check scheme selection and complete all required fields; missing compulsory responses may invalidate your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save progress and multi-session editing
rubrics_metrics.description: You can log in and out and complete your application over a number of days, make sure you save your progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the save feature and return to refine answers; do not leave final submission to last minute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special arrangements and contact email
rubrics_metrics.description: Any special arrangements need to be highlighted to the URF grants team URF@royalsociety.org. Any queries do not use the grants@royalsociety.org included on flexi-grant use URF@royalsociety.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct scheme-specific queries and requests for special arrangements to the URF grants team email provided, not the generic grants contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexi-grant technical support
rubrics_metrics.description: https://support.flexigrant.com/support/home can help with technical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the flexi-grant support portal for site-specific technical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stick to word counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Stick to the word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to stated word limits for sections; excess text may be disallowed or truncated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reminder about institutional approval timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember you have to submit this for approval by your organisation - give them enough time! Speak to your departmental administrator. The deadline is for the complete submission, not the submission to your departmental administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal approvals can take time; allow sufficient lead time so institutional approvers can review and submit before the funder's deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission completion responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure you remind participants to mark their work as complete and click submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts of the application (referees/HoD/approver) must mark and submit their sections; coordinate with them to confirm completion prior to the deadline.
